summary: Closes the remaining half of the myidsan productization plan's Phase 4 resource-limits item (4.3): runtime log rotation was previously by calendar day only, so one chatty or hostile day could fill the disk long before logging.cleanup.maxRetentionDays -- which deletes whole days -- became relevant. infra/logging now supports a per-file size cap: a new logging.maxFileSizeMb config key (0/negative = uncapped, the historic behaviour, wired through infra/config and infra/apphost's buildRuntimeLogger) rolls the active file to <name>-<date>.<n>.log once the cap is hit, resuming at the highest unfilled sequence on restart rather than reopening and overflowing an already-full file. Because retention discovers deletable files through logFiles() and dateValueFromPath(), both were changed in the same commit so a rotated file is never left undeletable: logFiles() gained a second glob for the sequenced shape, and dateValueFromPath() strips a suffix from the date component only when that suffix is entirely digits, so a lookalike name such as <name>-<date>.bak.log is still rejected rather than swept up and deleted. This is mutation-guarded by a new TestSizeRotatedFilesAreStillPruned (reverting only the parser half makes it delete 1 of 3 seeded files instead of 3). All four shipped deploy/dist/*-config.json now default logging.maxFileSizeMb to 100, since an uncapped default is what created this gap. Found and fixed in passing while touching this file: the runtime-log viewer's newest-first ordering (fileLogger.List) tie-broke same-second entries by string-comparing the RFC3339 Time field, which is wrong on two counts -- Go trims trailing fraction zeros so '.1Z' can string-compare greater than '.1000001Z', and on Windows the clock is coarse enough that adjacent writes get a byte-identical Time, leaving ties unresolved so the stable sort silently returned them oldest-first. This made TestFileLoggerWritesAndListsNewestFirst fail on Windows roughly 90% of the time (37/40 measured runs) while passing on Linux CI, which is why it went unnoticed. Ordering is now derived from append (read) order alone, needs no clock, and cannot tie (0/40 failures after the fix).
compatibility: This is shared infra (infra/logging, infra/config, infra/apphost) touched once for all four apps, not an app-specific change. Existing installs are unaffected until they explicitly set logging.maxFileSizeMb -- omitting it (as every pre-existing config does) keeps the exact prior uncapped, day-only rotation with no filename change. The shipped deploy/dist/*-config.json examples now default to 100 MB, so fresh installs/reinstalls from those templates get the cap; sequence-0 filenames (<name>-<date>.log) are byte-identical to before, so no existing log file is renamed, orphaned, or made unreadable by retention. The log-ordering fix changes the display order of same-second entries in the runtime log viewer (previously silently backwards on Windows in the tied case) but touches no API contract, storage format, or config.
